C · Why greedy’s answer cannot change — and the checks that it did not
untrained models of the real size, random sentences

The proof is two lines. A kept token is the model’s own greedy pick at its place, computed from exactly the tokens greedy would have written before it. A rejected guess is replaced by that same pick. So every token written is greedy’s, in order. The one place where the two can differ is arithmetic: one pass over
in a different order than two passes over
could swap — none did in any of these runs.

It changes no answer, so whether it helps is a question of what it costs and saves — and that depends on the hardware and the length of the text more than on training. The overview page puts all eight changes side by side.
